packet.title: near-approval spec review
packet.summary: What a spec reviewer reads and signs to discharge ASM-SPEC for the NEAR approval contract. The reviewer certifies that the specs say what the contract is meant to do: the property statements and the reference step semantics. The proofs re-run in CI on every change; the reviewer reads statements and skips proof bodies.
packet.qualifies: A named human who did not write approval-core. Claude sessions wrote most of the specs and harnesses, so a review by Claude does not count.
why_a_day: The step semantics is written four times (Prolog step/4, TLA+, Lean, the Verus spec machine) and machines check that the copies agree: MC-3 and MC-4 (Prolog graph = TLC graph = Lean graph, 21,670 stores, 41,706 edges); MC-2, RT-TRACE and REF-5 (210 traces, 6,800 steps, identical on the real core, spec.rs, tla.rs and the deployed wasm); Verus (the core refines abs.rs for every public function).

So the reviewer reads one copy of the step semantics closely (item C) and spot-checks the rest. Property statements are tied together only by shared IDs, C-7 traceability and mutants, so those are what need reading.

items.title: Contract intent (README)
items.summary: The contract README is the statement of intent. Everything in the later items must agree with it.
check: You understand what each of the 16 #[near] methods is for, who may call it, and what it records.
Nothing in the README is ambiguous enough that two readers would build different contracts.

items.title: Threats and property catalogue
items.summary: strategy.md section 3 (threats, trust assumptions) and section 5 (the property catalogue in math). Each property must mean what the README means.
check: Each property in section 5 states what the README means; none over-claims or under-claims.
Nothing the README promises is missing from section 5.
Section 3.2 maps every listed threat to at least one property.

items.title: Reference step semantics (Prolog step/4)
items.summary: The requirements-only Prolog machine. The TLC and Lean state graphs are machine-checked equal to it, and its traces are replayed on the real core and the wasm, so this is the one copy of the step semantics to read closely.
check: The guard order and the error each guard raises match the README for add_agent/add_approver, revoke_key, request_action, approve and reject.
The effects of each successful step (what is written, what counters move) match the README.

items.title: Verus spec machine and lemma statements
items.summary: The strongest evidence: a proof on the real core at every store size. Read abs.rs in full and only the ensures clauses (statements) of the lemma files.
check: The spec machine in abs.rs matches step/4 (item C).
Each lemma statement matches its section 5 row.

items.title: What Verus takes on trust
items.summary: Every assume_specification, external type spec and trusted impl the verified twin relies on, and every rewrite of deployed code inside the twin.
check: Each trusted std/near-sdk spec holds for the pinned toolchain and near-sdk 5.29.1.
Each rewrite is behaviour-preserving (each has a Kani equivalence harness).

read.label: Trusted specs, each mapped to an ASM

items.title: TLA+ property statements
items.summary: The TLA+ invariants, action properties and liveness formulas.
check: INV, HIST and liveness formulas match their section 5 rows.

items.title: Lean property statements and temporal encoding
items.summary: Lean proves the TLA+ model's properties at every size. Read the statements and the one-line encodings of the TLA+ temporal operators.
check: The Lean statements say what the TLA+ ones say.
Steps, EvAlways, InfOften, Enabled, WeakFair and StrongFair match TLA+ semantics.

read.label: Temporal encoding (Steps, EvAlways, InfOften, Enabled, WeakFair, StrongFair) and Live1

items.title: Kani executable spec (spec.rs)
items.summary: Kani checks the deployed code path within bounds, and L2 lifts that to every store size. Mostly redundant with D1; skim it.
check: expected agrees with step/4 (spot-check 3 operations).

items.title: Trust assumptions
items.summary: Every assumption the verification rests on, against strategy.md section 3.3. ASM-FINAL, ASM-TOOLS, ASM-OWNER and ASM-DISPLAY are trusted permanently by decision.
check: Each assumption is acceptable for this deployment.
The permanently trusted list (ASM-FINAL, ASM-TOOLS, ASM-OWNER, ASM-DISPLAY) is agreed.

items.title: near-sdk macro expansion (SH-9, RD-6)
items.summary: The #[near] wrapper is generated code that unit tests cannot see. Run cargo expand on the contract at the pin and read the wrapper.
check: #[init] new panics if state already exists, and is #[private].
Every method fails before init (PanicOnDefault).
Change methods are non-payable.
&self view methods never write state.
Only the 16 #[near] methods are exported.

items.title: Open findings accepted as documented
items.summary: Findings that stay open by design. Each is either defence in depth or covered by a property or deployment rule.
check: Each finding below is acceptable with the resolution path given.

C-1.description: Authority matrix: one authority per change method; owner/agent/approver method sets disjoint; no key can both request and approve

C-2.description: Guard table: every ApprovalError produced by >=1 guard; specified precedence equals generated code_precedence/2

C-3.description: Error messages pairwise distinct and substring-free

C-4.description: Each event from exactly one method; authority/proof-changing ops emit an event or carry accepted_risk (admin ops emit key_added / key_revoked since 3426c92)

C-5.description: Generated constants equal requirement constants; DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE <= MAX_PAGE_SIZE; MAX_PENDING_PER_KEY >= 1; MAX_ACTION_LEN within RES-2 bound

C-6.description: Generated API surface equals the requirements API table: #[near] wasm exports = method/3 names, other exports only near-sdk's (contract_source_metadata, __contract_abi), ABI kind and modifiers match each method's kind and authority

C-7.description: Traceability both ways: every requirement has >=1 property; every property traces to a requirement or threat

C-8.description: Every threat has mitigated_by or accepted_risk

C-9.description: Property and assumption IDs in status.toml equal those in traceability.pl

C-10.description: Warn when a verified* property depends on an assumption with level below high whose check has not passed

MC-1.description: Bounded model check of reference step/4 at depth 6 with real constants: no INV, separation-of-duties, double-approval, pending-count or revival violation; reaches approved and void states and every error except both LogFull and TooManyPending; MC-1s (max_pending=2, max_u=2) also reaches TooManyPending and request LogFull; state counts >= mc1_state_floor

MC-2.description: Generated traces replayed on the real core, on spec.rs and (RT-TRACE) on the wasm; all agree

C-2t.description: Guard table across models: TLA+ GuardOrder = guard/4 order = code_precedence/2

MC-3.description: Graph equivalence: Prolog step/4 and TLC export the full labelled reachable graph of one small universe; state and edge sets are equal

TX-0.description: Atomic failure: Err => state unchanged; no Store mutator on failure except remove_principal of an absent key (F-6, no-op)

TX-1.description: add_principal: Ok(principal) <=> caller = owner, key unregistered and G != MAXU; errors NotOwner, KeyAlreadyRegistered, LogFull; P' = P[k -> (acct, role, G, #R, 0)], G' = G + 1

TX-2.description: revoke_key: Ok(P(k)) <=> caller = owner and key registered; errors NotOwner, KeyNotRegistered; P' = P minus k, V' = V[P(k).reg -> t]

TX-3.description: authenticate: Ok <=> predecessor = signer and key registered to signer with role; errors IndirectCall, UnknownKey, WrongRole, KeyAccountMismatch; read-only

TX-4.description: request_action: exact result, error order (auth, EmptyAction, ActionTooLong, TooManyPending, LogFull), appended request recording the caller's registration id, caller key pend+1

TX-5.description: approve: exact result, error order (auth, RequestNotFound, AlreadyApproved, AlreadyRejected, AgentRevoked, ActionMismatch, SelfApproval, LogFull), approval recorded with the approver's registration id, log appended, agent key pend-1, proof = approval(s', i)

TX-7.description: reject: exact result, error order (auth, RequestNotFound, AlreadyApproved, AlreadyRejected, AgentRevoked, SelfApproval), rejection recorded with the approver's registration id, agent key pend-1, log unchanged; Ok(R'[i])

TX-6.description: Owner never changes; owner checks compare the caller account passed by the shell (predecessor: SH-1)

INV-0.description: Registry is a function: one registration and role per key (MemStore has no duplicate keys)

INV-3.description: Log -> request: L[j] < #R and R[L[j]] approved with index j

INV-4.description: Request -> log: approved R[i] has index < #L and L[index] = i

INV-5.description: Separation of duties: approver account != agent account, on every approval and rejection

INV-6.description: Approver key != agent key on every approval and rejection

INV-8.description: Registration provenance: R[i].ak = k and i >= P(k).active_from => R[i].aa = P(k).account, role Agent and R[i].agent_registration_id = P(k).registration_id

INV-9.description: Pending count: P(k).pending equals undecided (neither approved nor rejected) requests of k under its registration, <= 16 (0 for approvers); the cap bound is stepped in h_raw_request

INV-10.description: Time order (non-decreasing time inputs): approved_at and rejected_at >= requested_at component-wise

INV-11.description: Live registration ids are issued (< G), pairwise distinct and not revoked

INV-12.description: Revoked registration ids are issued (< G) and each is revoked once (insert_revocation's write-once law holds)

INV-13.description: At most one decision per request: never both approved and rejected

INV-14.description: Recorded registration ids (request agent, approver, rejecter) are issued (< G)

INV-15.description: Registration accounting: #P + #V = G, so with INV-11/12 every issued registration is exactly one of live or revoked

INV-16.description: Registration binding: a live registration id recorded on a request or decision belongs to the key, account and role it was recorded with

LEM-3.description: An unapproved request exists => #L < #R <= MAXU, so approve's LogFull is unreachable (F-7)

LEM-4.description: Under INV-8, liveness reduces to active_from <= id; role/account checks are redundant (F-14, the 2 equivalent mutants)

HIST-1.description: Request content immutable and never removed

HIST-2.description: Decisions immutable once recorded: approvals and rejections

HIST-4.description: #R grows by 1 exactly on a successful request, #L by 1 exactly on a successful approval; otherwise unchanged

HIST-5.description: Proof stability: a published proof never changes

HIST-6.description: Registry discipline: owner fixed; P changes only by owner Add/Revoke or the pending field on request/approve/reject

HIST-7.description: Owner operations never change requests or the log, and reject never changes the log, from any state

HIST-10.description: Registrations and revocations: G grows by 1 exactly on a successful Add, V gains one entry exactly on a successful Revoke, and a recorded revocation never changes

TR-1.description: Provenance: every proof has a prior successful request by a registered agent key and a successful approval restating the action by a registered approver key of a different account, with the agent registration continuous in between; the proof's registration ids are the registrations in force at request and approval

TR-2.description: Each request decided (approved or rejected) at most once in any trace

TR-3.description: Durable revocation: a request whose agent registration is revoked while pending is never approved, even after re-registration

TR-4.description: Approval times non-decreasing along the log

TR-5.description: Non-vacuity: approved, rejected and void states reachable; every error reachable (approve LogFull only from a non-Inv Sparse state, h_proto_approve); request LogFull only at #R = MAXU

TR-6.description: Agent storage bound as a potential: Phi = sum over agent keys of (16 - pending) >= 0 drops by 1 per successful request and rises only on a successful approval or rejection or agent Add

TR-7.description: Revocation record: V lists exactly the successful Revokes, in order, each with the registration id it removed (as issued, fresh, by Add) and its time

RD-1.description: approval(s,i) = Some(proof(R[i])) iff approved; None for pending, void or unknown

RD-2.description: Exact page: approvals(f,l) = proofs of L[f..min(f saturating_add min(l,100), #L)], no drops

RD-3.description: Page arithmetic over any u64 (from, limit, count): no overflow; reads only approval_count, approved_request_id(j) in the page and request(id) for returned ids; no writes

RD-4.description: Client loop (stop on empty page or from >= count) enumerates the log exactly once, in order

RD-5.description: Per-request and paged views agree; proof findable by request_id or approval_index

RD-6.description: Core reads are pure (Window store panics on writes); every get_* takes &self

RD-7.description: request_status = Approved / Rejected / Pending (live) / Void; None for unknown ids

RD-8.description: proof_revocations(proof) = (V(agent registration), V(approver registration)); under Inv each is None exactly when that registration is still the key's current one

ROB-1.description: No panics, overflows or OOB indexing for any arguments and any MemStore within the bounds (beyond: ASM-MODEL), including non-Inv states

ROB-2.description: LogFull guards: count = MAXU with all earlier guards passing => Err(LogFull), no writes, before the shell's += 1 (which would panic under overflow-checks); approve's case needs a non-Inv state

ROB-3.description: Action length boundaries in bytes: 0, 1 (a space), 2048, 2049 and a multi-byte 2050

ROB-4.description: Bounded work: <= 4 Store reads and <= 3 writes per mutator; approvals <= 2*min(l,100)+1 reads

ST-1.description: Store laws for MemStore and Sparse (map/sequence semantics; removing an absent key is a no-op)

ST-2.description: Store protocol: exact mutator call sequence per op; makes contract-store differences from MemStore unreachable

ST-3.description: Sparse (transliteration of the contract Store impl) refines ArrStore under Kani (h_refine_*) and MemStore in plain mode; ST-1 laws tie ArrStore and MemStore to the same observations

ST-8.description: Store protocol at any store size (K-ORACLE): on a Sparse holding the step's footprint at any keys and positions, with every field and counter free, approve and reject return exactly expect() and make exactly the protocol() calls, with accounts from 8 values (ST-8W, src::Wide: every footprint maps injectively); add, revoke and request read no request, so h_proto_* already covers them at every size

TLA-SAFE.description: TLC: Inv (INV-3..9, INV-11..16, LEM-1/2, TR-1 provenance, RidLive, Approvable) in every reachable state and StepProperty (HIST-1/2/3/7/8/9/10, TR-2, TR-3) on every step, any interleaving of all calls by all parties

TLA-IND.description: Apalache: Init => Inv, and Inv /\ Next => Inv' /\ StepProps from any state with <= 3 requests, integers unbounded, MaxPending scaled to 2: Inv and the step properties hold at every depth

TLA-LIVE-1.description: Under weak fairness of approvers, a request whose eligible approver eventually always exists never stays pending (ends approved, rejected or void); fails without fairness (non-vacuity). MC_Liveness_SF: under strong fairness an eligible approver infinitely often is enough (TLA-LIVE-1s)

TLA-LIVE-2.description: Approvable: every Approver key of another account can approve or reject a pending request (no accepted request is stuck in the core)

TLA-WIT.description: Non-vacuity: approved, rejected, void, revival-attempt and pending-cap states are reachable in TLC; IndInit holds full states with approved, rejected and void requests and a revocation

REF-1.description: Guard exactness (A1): the core's error equals the TLA+ error operator on alpha(pre); Ok exactly when the TLA+ action is enabled

REF-2.description: Effect exactness (A2): on Ok, alpha(post) is the TLA+ action's post-state

REF-3.description: Rejected calls stutter (A3): on Err, alpha(post) = alpha(pre)

REF-4.description: Time irrelevance (A7): tla.rs reads no BlockTime, so REF-1/2 hold for every block time; payload classes (A5) via h_ref_toolong

REF-5.description: Trace validation: 60 x 80-call core traces equal tla.rs on every step, and TLC accepts each as a behaviour of ApprovalCore.tla (>= 5 revival attempts, >= 20 rejections and revocations)

CUT-1.description: Footprint (kani/CUTOFF.md): each call reads and writes at most the keys, request positions, log slots and revocation records of its row; tracking is transparent

CUT-2.description: Cutoff: given CUT-1, harness state bounds (CAP_P, CAP_R, CAP_V) are sufficient for REF-1..3 at every size, except E1 (pending at MAXP) and E2 (counters at u64::MAX), which raw and Sparse harnesses cover, including request/approve LogFull (h_proto_request, h_proto_approve)

U-1.description: Every loop in every harness's goto program has a bound derived from a constant, and no reachable loop needs more than its harness unwind

LEAN-IND.description: Lean: Init => Inv and Inv /\ Next => Inv' (TypeOK, INV-2..9, INV-11..16, INV-5r, LEM-1/2, TR-1 provenance, RidLive, Approvable) for states of every size, every MaxPending, any key, account and payload types; so Inv holds in every reachable state. TLA-IND without its bound of 3

LEAN-STEP.description: Lean: every call from an Inv state, successful or not, satisfies StepProps (HIST-1/2/3/7/8/9/10), at every size

LEAN-TR.description: Lean: over every run of any length from a reachable state, a decision is final (TR-2), Void is terminal across revoke and re-add (TR-3), request content, the log prefix, the registration counter and the revocation set only grow; every decided request has TR-1 provenance

LEAN-GUARD.description: Lean: each error operator returns the first failing guard of a list whose codes are TLA+'s GuardOrder (equal to tla_facts.pl, C-2t); LogFull is never returned (A6)

LEAN-WIT.description: Non-vacuity: reachable states with an approved, a rejected, a void and a revoked-re-added-still-void request and a key at the pending cap, checked by evaluation

LEAN-LIVE.description: Lean: TLA-LIVE-1 for every behaviour at every size (any key, account and payload types, any MaxPending, any number of requests and registrations, any step relation, so both Next and MC_Liveness's BNext); TLA-LIVE-1s under strong fairness; a concrete unfair behaviour violates Live1 and a fair one satisfies its premise. TLA-LIVE-1 without TLC's bounds

REF-5L.description: The real core's MC-2 traces (2000 x 120 calls) replayed on the Lean machine: every result and post-store equal

LEAN-DELTA.description: Lean: on every concrete store of every size whose request ids equal their positions and whose counters are below u64::MAX, the transcribed expect error is the model's err and running the transcribed protocol calls lands on the model's step, up to map equality of principals and set equality of revocations

LINK.description: ghost::expect / ghost::protocol (Rust) equal the Lean cstep on the representative view of every class (14,310 views, Lean's allCls.map rep exactly, as a set); the real core on a Sparse holding each view agrees too

LEAN-COVER.description: Lean: for every footprint view of every concrete store (any identity types, any Nat counters, request at i has id i and a pay action), cls v is in allCls and cstep v op = (sub v op).out (cstep (rep (cls v op))): every view steps like its LINK representative, transported back

LEAN-FRAME.description: Lean: cstep depends only on the footprint (owner, call key's principal, request at the id, its key's principal, decision ids, counters): stores agreeing there step the same

LEAN-REN.description: Lean: cstep commutes with renaming accounts, keys and payloads, for any renaming injective on the footprint

K-LINK-T.description: Rust side of LEAN-COVER: on a symbolic footprint view (any u8 accounts and keys, free u64/u32 counters and times), ghost::expect / ghost::protocol on the view equal the transported result of the same functions on its representative

MC-4.description: Graph equivalence: the Lean machine and TLC export the full labelled reachable graph of the MC_Graph universe; stores, rejected calls and edges are equal (with MC-3: Prolog = TLC = Lean)

ST-4.description: Real ApprovalContract store (public methods, mocked runtime) refines MemStore over 10k x 50 random ops, persisted and reloaded every step: equal results and alpha after every step

ST-5.description: Storage prefixes p/r/a/v pairwise distinct, prefix-free and distinct from STATE; after every random step the keys are exactly STATE and prefix ++ borsh(key) for the entries alpha lists

ST-6.description: Golden Borsh bytes (key, value) for STATE and one entry of each map: ed25519 and secp256k1 principals; pending, approved, rejected requests; log entry; revocation. Layout changes flagged storage-breaking

ST-7.description: Identity equality: == on near-sdk AccountId and PublicKey equals Borsh-byte equality, is reflexive and symmetric, and survives clone and a Borsh round trip (edge identities and 200k random pairs); the checked half of ASM-IDENT

SH-1.description: Env mapping (caller, now) with pairwise-distinct context values; add_agent/add_approver pass the right role; all three owner methods pass the predecessor (DAO owner works, relayed owner signature fails)

SH-2.description: Exactly one core transition per change call and no other writes

SH-3.description: Core Err(e) panics with exactly e.as_str() (catch_unwind; payload HostError(GuestPanic { panic_msg })) and logs nothing; all 17 errors incl. the three LogFull guards

SH-4.description: approval_requested: exactly one NEP-297 line with RequestView(r), status pending; emitted only after Ok

SH-5.description: action_approved: exactly one line; data = return value = get_approval(i) at approval (revocation fields null); later get_approval differs only in agent_key_revoked_at / approver_key_revoked_at

SH-6.description: Each change method logs exactly its one event (key_added, key_revoked with voided_pending, approval_requested, action_approved, action_rejected = returned RejectionView); new, views and failed calls log nothing

SH-7.description: View mapping: get_approval(s) with proof_revocations, get_approvals defaults (0, 50); get_request None past #R else every field of R[i] plus request_status; get_rejection; get_revocation = V(g); get_principal None if unregistered else account, role, registration_id, pending; get_owner; counts

SH-8.description: JSON shape: README field names of every view and event payload (incl. revocation fields, RejectionView, KeyView, KeyRevokedView, BlockTimeView), U64 strings for *_ns, numbers for ids and heights, {} or null fields give defaults, whole-args null fails (wasm wrappers: sandbox), lossless conversions

SH-9.description: Init once, only from C; methods fail before init; post-init state is Init(owner)

SH-10.description: All 16 exports at the pin (F-15; the row said 13) called with 1 yocto via full-access keys (new on a fresh deployment): every change method and new fail with the non-payable panic; observed: every get_* (and contract_source_metadata) accepts the deposit

SH-11.description: Function exports exactly the 16 #[near] methods + contract_source_metadata + __contract_abi (embedded by cargo-near); the only non-function export is memory; no Store, upgrade or owner-transfer export

SH-13.description: add_agent and add_approver refuse ML-DSA-65 keys (F-17): after the owner check (non-owners get NotOwner) and before the core's guards (LogFull), with exactly UNSUPPORTED_KEY_TYPE and no log; so every registered key is ed25519 or secp256k1, the key types RES-1 and RES-2 bound

SH-12.description: No promise_*, deploy, delete, add-key, global-contract or transfer imports (exact import set in wasm-surface.expected); only ST-5 storage keys written

RES-1.description: Storage growth per op (add, revoke, request, approve, reject) computed from the Borsh layout and equal to VMLogic's metering at the worst case; measured on-chain (sandbox); 16 x B_req = 0.364 NEAR per agent key without an approver (ed25519/secp256k1; ML-DSA-65 keys are refused, SH-13)

RES-2.description: Worst-case approval_requested, action_approved and action_rejected lines (2048 escaped control bytes, 64-char accounts, ed25519/secp256k1 keys, max u64s) fit 16384 B: 13197 B (F-4). ML-DSA-65 keys, which would reach 18256 B on both sides (F-17), cannot be registered (SH-13)

RES-3.description: get_approvals(0,100) over 100 max-size proofs stays under view gas and 4 MiB return; measured about 1.30 MB (1,299,658-1,299,659 B) and about 88.3-88.4 TGas as a transaction (near-sandbox 2.13.4)

RT-KEY.description: FC key of account a arrives as signer = predecessor = a with signer_pk = key; unregistered and cross-account keys rejected

RT-RELAY.description: Calls through a third-party relay contract fail IndirectCall

RT-SELFACCT.description: A contract on the signer's own account calling C succeeds (documents F-9)

RT-METATX.description: NEP-366 delegate action outcome recorded: IndirectCall on C for both an agent function-call key and a full-access agent key (results/RT-METATX.json)

RT-FCKEY.description: Agent FC key scoped to request_action cannot call approve or add_agent: InvalidAccessKeyError(MethodNameMismatch), not a contract panic

RT-REVERT.description: Forced failures (core panic, out of gas after the emit, LackBalanceForState on request and approve) leave state and views unchanged; observed: the event survives in the failed outcome for out-of-gas and LackBalanceForState (results/RT-REVERT.json)

RT-BATCH.description: Batched [request_action(a), request_action('')] signed by a full-access registered agent key fails at action 1 and leaves counters unchanged; observed: the first action's approval_requested event appears in the failed outcome

RT-RESET.description: Delete + recreate C resets counters; VER-3 detects it (VER-6 only heuristically)

RT-SPOOF.description: Forged EVENT_JSON from a spoofer contract rejected by the VER-1 executor_id rule

RT-TIME.description: Stored request/approval/rejection times equal the block their receipt ran in; heights strictly increase and timestamps never decrease across receipts on C

RT-CODEHASH.description: Wasm under test is the reproducible build; record sha256 (hex) and NEAR code_hash (base58)

RT-TRACE.description: Prolog traces + 200 random sequences replayed on the reproducible wasm equal spec.rs: results, exact messages, logs, views

DEP-1.description: Code hash = reproducible build, not a global contract referenced by account id; locked at deploy (deploy + new + full-access key deletion in one tx); owner is multisig/DAO; registered keys (rebuilt from an indexer) are FC keys scoped to C ([request_action]; [approve] or [approve, reject]) with finite allowance; balance buffer. Demonstrated on near-sandbox only: no testnet deployment

VER-1.description: Accept proofs only from get_approval at final, or action_approved logs of successful receipts with executor_id = C in final blocks

VER-2.description: code_hash(C) = expected at the proof's block (archival) and now

VER-3.description: No full-access key on C since b0, or an indexer scan finds no DeployContract/UseGlobalContract/AddKey/DeleteAccount

VER-4.description: Check action and both accounts against expectations; approver against the verifier's own allowlist

VER-5.description: Enumerate with the RD-4 loop at one block_id

VER-6.description: Counter decrease or code-hash change invalidates cached proofs

VER-7.description: Executors deduplicate on (C, request_id) and enforce a maximum approval age

VER-8.description: Per proof: archival view_access_key for the agent key at the request block and the approver key at the approval block both show a function-call permission with receiver C and the DEP-1 method names (closes F-9)

ASM-SIGNER.statement: signer_account_pk() is the key whose signature over the originating tx was verified, an access key of signer_account_id(); signatures unforgeable

ASM-PRED.statement: predecessor_account_id() is unforgeable; equals the signer for the first receipt and when code on the signer's own account calls (F-9)

ASM-ATOMIC.statement: Atomicity is per receipt: panic, out-of-gas or LackBalanceForState reverts all writes, including earlier actions batched in the same receipt; logs of a failed receipt may remain

ASM-SEQ.statement: Receipts on one account execute one at a time; the contract creates no promises, so no reentrancy; each successful action is one model step

ASM-TIME.statement: block_height and block_timestamp never decrease across receipts on one account

ASM-FINAL.statement: State at finality 'final' is never reverted

ASM-CODE.statement: Code changes only via DeployContract or UseGlobalContract on C (both need a full-access key on C), or via DeployGlobalContract by the owner of a NEP-591 global contract C references by account id; DeleteAccount erases state and a recreated account starts empty

ASM-SDK.statement: #[init] panics if state exists; #[private] requires predecessor = current account; non-payable change methods reject deposits; &self never writes; only #[near] impl methods exported; PanicOnDefault blocks default init

ASM-STORE.statement: store::LookupMap is a map keyed prefix ++ borsh(key); writes flushed when the contract struct drops after state_write. For M5 path A: the contract crate's Store impl meets the Store trait's Verus contract (verified for MemStore; tested, not proved, for the NEAR store)

ASM-IDENT.statement: PartialEq on AccountId/PublicKey is an equivalence matching Borsh-byte equality; the core uses A/K only via Clone and PartialEq (parametricity: a footprint maps injectively into the harness identities, ST-8W); harnesses use opaque newtypes so a new trait bound breaks the build. Which views LINK covers is no longer part of it (LEAN-COVER, K-LINK-T)

ASM-STAKE.statement: Account must hold storage_usage * 1e19 yocto; ~40 B overhead per record

ASM-LIMITS.statement: max_total_log_length 16384 B; 100 logs; 4 MiB return data; 300 TGas per call; view gas cap per node

ASM-META.statement: NEP-366 (and NEP-518 eth-implicit) inner receipts carry the relayer as signer, so relayed calls fail IndirectCall

ASM-FCKEY.statement: Function-call keys restrict receiver and methods, cannot attach deposits, have an allowance, and cannot add keys

ASM-COMPILE.statement: rustc/LLVM/wasm-opt preserve core semantics host -> wasm32; overflow-checks on in release; the only on-chain usize use is action.len() > MAX_ACTION_LEN; cfg(feature="borsh") gates only use/derive

ASM-MODEL.statement: Kani-layer properties only: a core step on a state larger than the Kani bound behaves like one within it (strategy section 6.3). Properties on the verus layer (M5 path A) are proved on the real core at every size and do not rely on it

ASM-TLA-SCOPE.statement: TLA+ model bounds (strategy section 17.3): behaviours with more requests, keys or accounts than TLC and Apalache explore add no new violations. Accounts and keys are covered by ASM-IDENT parametricity; the request bound is a small-scope assumption. It backs no every-size claim: LEAN-IND, LEAN-STEP and LEAN-TR prove the safety properties and LEAN-LIVE proves TLA-LIVE-1/1s at every size (strategy sections 18.3, 18.7). It remains only as the scope of the TLC and Apalache rows themselves

ASM-LEAN-TLA.statement: The Lean machine (lean/ApprovalLean/Machine.lean, Props.lean) transcribes ApprovalCore.tla and ApprovalProps.tla, and Liveness.lean transcribes MC_Liveness.tla with TLA+'s temporal operators over behaviours Nat -> State (strategy sections 18, 18.7)

ASM-SPEC.statement: spec.rs, the Verus specs and the Prolog requirements state the intended behaviour; signed off by a human who did not write approval-core

ASM-TOOLS.statement: Kani (unwinding assertions on), Verus+Z3, scryer-prolog, TLC, Apalache and the Lean 4 kernel are sound at the pinned versions

ASM-OWNER.statement: The owner registers keys honestly (it could otherwise register two accounts it controls)

ASM-DEPLOY.statement: The deployed code is the reproducible build of the pin, locked at deploy

ASM-DISPLAY.statement: Approver UIs render the action text faithfully (the approve tx commits to the text itself)

ASM-NU.statement: The Rust (kani/src/norm.rs) and Lean (lean/ApprovalLean/Ident.lean) transcriptions of LINK's class, representative and transport functions agree (strategy section 18.6.1)

ASM-STRLEN.statement: (M5 only) String::len is the UTF-8 byte length; is_empty <=> len == 0

ASM-DERIVE.statement: (M5 only) #[derive(Clone)] clones field-wise and #[derive(PartialEq)] on Role compares variants; the twin declares these for the core's data types (verus/TRUSTED.toml), which stay outside verus! so their derives are untouched

ASM-IDTYPE.statement: (M5 only) On near_sdk::AccountId and near_sdk::PublicKey, == is structural equality and clone returns an equal value (the eq_laws / clone_laws hypotheses every Verus core function requires); the equivalence half of ASM-IDENT without its parametricity half

F-4.finding: `MAX_ACTION_LEN` is coupled to the 16 KiB log limit. The worst-case `action_approved` line is about 13.0 KB (2048 control bytes escaped to `\u00XX`, 64-char accounts, secp256k1 keys, max `u64`s). The limit breaks above about 2.6 KB. Upstream has a doc comment but no test.

F-6.finding: `revoke_key` calls `remove_principal` before knowing the key exists. The core's "no writes on `Err`" holds only because removing an absent key is a no-op (L-REMOVE-ABSENT). On-chain the call panics before any flush, so nothing is written.
F-6.resolution: ST-2 records it. Optionally reorder upstream (OQ-5).

F-7.finding: `approve`'s `LogFull` branch is unreachable under `Inv`: a pending request implies `#L < #R ≤ MAXU`.
F-7.resolution: Kept as defence in depth. LEM-3.

F-9.finding: `predecessor == signer` also admits code deployed on the signer's own account.
F-9.resolution: DEP-1 requires registered keys to be function-call keys with receiver `C`. RT-SELFACCT.

F-10.finding:
**formalver tooling defects:**
(a) `run-prolog.sh` ends with `\|\| true` and runs `-g "run_tests, halt."`; a failing `run_tests` falls through to the toplevel, which exits 0 at EOF. Failures never fail the script.
(b) `run-verus.sh` and the README's direct `verus` command omit `--cfg 'feature="verus"'`, so ironclaw's `cfg(feature="verus")` spec and proof modules are never compiled [conf: high]. The README's `./tools/get-z3.sh` lives under `source/` in the Verus repo.
(c) ironclaw proofs take their conclusion as a `requires`.
(d) ironclaw's gitlink `d313f44` ≠ recorded pin `34550ad`.
(e) No CI.
F-10.resolution: M0 fixed (a) and (e). M5 fixed (b): `run-verus.sh` always passes the cfg, so ironclaw's Verus code now compiles and fails (it predates vstd's current API; out of scope). (d): `check-pin.sh` is per project and CI runs it for near-approval only (OQ-6). Rule for this project: no proof assumes its conclusion.

F-15.finding: PR #15 changes the shell: a `reject` method, `action_rejected`, `key_added` and `key_revoked` events, `agent_key_revoked_at` / `approver_key_revoked_at` on proof views, `get_revocation`, and a `v` storage prefix for revocations. SH-4..SH-8, SH-10, SH-11 (export count: 16 at `main`, the row said 13), C-4, ST-5, RES-1 and requirement D11 ("no rejection") described the `5736251` shell.
F-15.resolution: **Done at M3** (2026-10-15): those rows, their `traceability.pl` and `status.toml` descriptions, and C-6's check describe the PR #15 shell; D11 reads "no upgrade, ownership transfer, expiry or threshold" and D17 covers rejection.

F-17.finding: near-sdk-core 4.2.3 (in the lockfile) accepts **ML-DSA-65** public keys (1952 bytes; nearcore 2.13, protocol 85). With ML-DSA-65 keys on both sides, the worst-case `action_approved` line is 18256 B, over the 16384 B limit: the core accepts the request, and that approver key can never approve it (the call fails with `TotalLogLengthExceeded`). One ML-DSA-65 key on either side still fits (≤ 15775 B), so another approver with a shorter key can. Storage per request also grows (`B_req` 4160 B; 16 pending = 0.666 NEAR). The README's worst case assumes secp256k1.
F-17.resolution: **Fixed upstream** in trust-framework PR #19 (pin `081a3a6`, 2026-10-17): `add_agent`/`add_approver` refuse ML-DSA-65 keys after the owner check. Checked by SH-13 (`f17_mldsa65_keys_are_refused`). Supporting them later needs a shorter event or a lower action limit (README).

F-16.finding: `insert_revocation` is "written at most once per id" by contract, and the stores disagree otherwise: `MemStore` keeps the first write, the contract's `LookupMap` the last. The core writes `P(k).reg` on revoke, which INV-11 keeps out of `V`, so the case is unreachable from `Init`.
F-16.resolution: INV-11/INV-12 prove the law holds on reachable states. ST-2 records the call.

F-14.finding: Two equivalent mutants. In `live_agent_registration`, dropping the role check or the account check survives all tests: under INV-8 both are implied by `active_from ≤ id`. They are kept as defence in depth.
F-14.resolution: LEM-4 proves the redundancy, so the equivalence is established and not merely assumed.
